verses.text: This na the family record of Jesus the Messiah—David’s son, Abraham’s son too. 🌿
Abraham fathered Isaac; Isaac fathered Jacob; Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
Judah and Tamar had Perez and Zerah. Perez became Hezron’s father, and Hezron became Ram’s.
Ram fathered Amminadab; Amminadab fathered Nahshon; Nahshon fathered Salmon.
Salmon and Rahab had Boaz; Boaz and Ruth had Obed; Obed became Jesse’s father.
Jesse became King David’s father. David the king fathered Solomon through the woman who had been Uriah’s wife.
Solomon fathered Rehoboam; Rehoboam fathered Abijah; Abijah fathered Asa.
Asa fathered Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat fathered Joram; Joram fathered Uzziah.
Uzziah fathered Jotham; Jotham fathered Ahaz; Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh; Manasseh fathered Amon; Amon fathered Josiah.
Josiah became Jechoniah and his brothers’ father around the time Israel was carried off to Babylon.
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud; Abiud fathered Eliakim; Eliakim fathered Azor.
Azor fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Achim; Achim fathered Eliud.
Eliud fathered Eleazar; Eleazar fathered Matthan; Matthan fathered Jacob.
Jacob fathered Joseph, Mary’s husband. Mary gave birth to Jesus, the one called the Messiah.
So, count am: Abraham to David, fourteen generations; David to the exile in Babylon, fourteen; the exile to the Messiah, fourteen.
Here’s how Jesus the Messiah was born: Mary his mother was engaged to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, was a righteous man. He didn’t want to put her on blast in public, so he planned to end the engagement quietly.

As he was turning it over in his mind, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She’ll give birth to a son. Name him Jesus, because he’s the one who will save his people from their sins.” ✨
All this happened so what the Lord spoke through the prophet would come true:
“Look—the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son. They’ll call his name Immanuel,” which means, “God with us.”
Joseph woke up and did what the Lord’s angel commanded him; he took Mary as his wife.
He had no sexual relations with her before she gave birth to her firstborn son. Joseph named him Jesus.
Jesus was born in Bethlehem, Judea, while Herod was king. Around then, some wise men from the east pulled into Jerusalem.
“Where is the child born to be King of the Jews? We saw his star rise in the east, and we came to worship him.”
When King Herod heard that, he was shaken—and Jerusalem was shaken right along with him.
He gathered all the chief priests and teachers of the law and asked them where the Messiah was to be born.
They told him, “In Bethlehem, Judea. The prophet wrote:
‘Bethlehem, in Judah’s land, you are by no means the least among Judah’s rulers. From you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men in and got the exact time the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem: “Go and search carefully for the child. When you find him, report back to me so I can go worship him too.”
They heard the king and set out. The star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, joy hit them hard—they were overjoyed! 🌟
They went into the house and saw the child with Mary his mother. They bowed down and worshiped him; then they opened their treasures and gave him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
They were warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they returned to their own country by another route.

After they left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream: “Get up. Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there till I tell you, because Herod is about to search for the child and kill him.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother that night, and left for Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod died. That fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: “I called my son out of Egypt.”

Herod realized the wise men had outsmarted him, and he was furious. He sent men to kill every boy in Bethlehem and its surrounding area who was two years old or younger, using the exact time he had learned from the wise men.
Then what Jeremiah the prophet had said came true:
“A cry was heard in Ramah—people grieving, weeping, and mourning deeply. Rachel was weeping for her children; nobody could comfort her, because they were gone.”
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt.
“Get up. Take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel,” the angel said, “because the people trying to kill the child are dead.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and went to Israel.
But he heard that Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, and he was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he went away to the region of Galilee.
He settled in a town called Nazareth. That fulfilled what the prophets had said: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
Around that time, John the Baptizer showed up preaching in Judea’s wilderness:
“Turn back to God—Heaven’s Kingdom is close!”
Isaiah the prophet was talking about John when he said: “A voice is shouting in the wilderness: Get the Lord’s road ready; make his paths straight!”
John wore clothes made from camel’s hair, tied with a leather belt. His food? Locusts and wild honey. 🍯
People came out to him from Jerusalem, all over Judea, and the whole region around the Jordan.
They were baptized by him in the Jordan River as they confessed their sins.
But when John saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said, “You bunch of snakes! Who tipped you off to run from the coming wrath?
So let your lives show the fruit that matches repentance!
Don’t start telling yourselves, ‘Abraham is our father.’ I’m telling you: God can raise children for Abraham from these stones.
The ax is already at the trees’ roots. Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit gets cut down and thrown into the fire.”
“I baptize you in water for repentance. But the one coming after me is stronger than I am; I’m not even worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, ready to clear his threshing floor. He’ll gather the wheat into his barn, but burn the chaff with fire that won’t go out.”
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to be baptized by John.
John tried to stop him: “I’m the one who needs to be baptized by you, and you’re coming to me?”
Jesus answered him, “Let it happen for now. This is the right way for us to fulfill all righteousness.” So John let him.
After Jesus was baptized, he came straight up out of the water. Look—the heavens opened, and he saw God’s Spirit coming down like a dove and settling on him. 🕊️
A voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son. I’m well pleased with him.”
Then the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness so the devil could test him.
He fasted forty days and forty nights. After all that, hunger finally hit.
The tempter came up and said, “If you’re God’s Son, tell these stones to become bread.”
Jesus answered, “Scripture says, ‘A person doesn’t live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from God’s mouth.’”
Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the highest point of the temple.
“If you’re God’s Son, jump down,” he said. “Scripture says, ‘He’ll command his angels about you,’ and, ‘They’ll carry you in their hands so you don’t strike your foot on a stone.’”
Jesus told him, “Scripture also says, ‘Don’t test the Lord your God.’”
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him every kingdom in the world and all their glory.
“I’ll give you all this,” he said, “if you bow down and worship me.”
Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan! Scripture says, ‘Worship the Lord your God, and serve him only.’”
Then the devil left him, and angels came to serve him. 👼
When Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he went back to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the regions of Zebulun and Naphtali.
That fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah had said:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan—Galilee of the Gentiles—
the people sitting in darkness saw a great light; on those sitting in death’s shadow, light has dawned.”
From then on, Jesus began preaching: “Turn back to God! Heaven’s Kingdom is close!”
Walking beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers: Simon, also called Peter, and his brother Andrew. They were fishermen, casting a net into the sea. 🎣
He said to them, “Come follow me. I’ll teach you to fish for people.”
Right away, they left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw two more brothers: James, Zebedee’s son, and John his brother. They were in a boat with Zebedee their father, repairing their nets. Jesus called them.
At once they left the boat and their father, and followed him.
Jesus traveled all through Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

News about him spread through all Syria. People brought him everyone who was sick or suffering from diseases and severe pain, people tormented by demons, those having seizures, and those who couldn’t move. Jesus healed them.
Huge crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and across the Jordan.
When Jesus saw the crowds, he went up the mountain and sat down. His disciples came over to him.
Then he began teaching them:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, because Heaven’s Kingdom belongs to them.
“Blessed are those who mourn; they will be comforted.
“Blessed are the gentle; they will inherit the earth.
“Blessed are those hungry and thirsty for righteousness; they will be filled.
“Blessed are the merciful; they will receive mercy.
“Blessed are the pure in heart; they will see God.
“Blessed are the peacemakers; they will be called God’s children.
“Blessed are those persecuted for doing what’s right, because Heaven’s Kingdom belongs to them.
“You’re blessed when people insult you, persecute you, and make up all kinds of evil stories about you because of me.
“Be glad—yes, celebrate! Your reward in heaven is great. They persecuted the prophets before you the same way. 🎉
“You are the earth’s salt. But if salt loses its flavor, how will it get salty again? It’s no good anymore; people throw it out and walk all over it.
“You are the world’s light. A city sitting on a hill can’t be hidden.
“Nobody lights a lamp and hides it under a measuring basket. They put it on a stand, and it lights up everyone in the house.
“In the same way, let your light shine in front of people. They’ll see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
“Don’t think I came to scrap the Law or the Prophets. I didn’t come to scrap them; I came to fulfill them.
“I’m telling you the truth: heaven and earth may pass away, but not even the smallest letter or tiny pen-stroke will disappear from the Law until everything is fulfilled.

“So whoever breaks even one of the least commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in Heaven’s Kingdom. But whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in Heaven’s Kingdom.
“I’m telling you, unless your righteousness goes beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, you won’t enter Heaven’s Kingdom.
“You heard what was said long ago: ‘Don’t murder.’ Whoever murders will face judgment.
“But I’m telling you: anyone angry with his brother without a cause will face judgment. Whoever says ‘Raca!’ will answer to the council; whoever says ‘You fool!’ faces the fire of Gehenna.
“So if you’re bringing your gift to the altar and remember your brother or sister has something against you,
“leave your gift there in front of the altar. Go make peace with them first, then come back and offer your gift.
“Settle things quickly with your accuser while you’re on the way to court. Otherwise, they may hand you to the judge, the judge to the officer, and you’ll end up in prison.
“I’m telling you the truth: you won’t get out until you’ve paid the last penny.
“You heard it said: ‘Don’t commit adultery.’
“But I’m telling you, whoever keeps looking at a woman with lust has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
“If your right eye trips you up, tear it out and throw it away. Better to lose one part of you than have your whole body thrown into Gehenna.
“If your right hand trips you up, cut it off and throw it away. Better to lose one part of you than have your whole body thrown into Gehenna.
“It was also said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
“But I’m telling you: anyone who divorces his wife, except because of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
“Again, you heard what was said long ago: ‘Don’t make false vows; keep the vows you make to the Lord.’
“But I’m telling you, don’t swear at all—not by heaven, because it’s God’s throne;
“not by the earth, because it’s the stool for his feet; not by Jerusalem, because it’s the city of the great King.
“And don’t swear by your own head—you can’t make one hair turn white or black.
“Let your ‘Yes’ mean yes, and your ‘No’ mean no. Anything beyond that comes from the evil one.
“You heard it said: ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
“But I’m telling you, don’t fight back against an evil person. If someone slaps your right cheek, turn the other one too.
“If someone sues you for your coat, let them have your cloak too.
“If someone forces you to go one mile, go two with them.
“Give to the person who asks you, and don’t turn away someone who wants to borrow from you.
“You heard it said: ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
“But I’m telling you: love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to people who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat and persecute you.
“Then you’ll be children of your Father in heaven. He makes the sun rise on evil people and good people, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
“If you love only people who love you, what reward is that? Even tax collectors do the same.
“If you greet only your friends, what’s special about that? Even tax collectors do the same.
“So be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.”
“Watch yourselves: don’t do good deeds in public just so people will notice. Do that, and your Father in heaven won’t reward you.

“When you give to people in need, don’t announce it with a trumpet like the hypocrites do in synagogues and on the streets to get people praising them. I’m telling you the truth: that applause is all the reward they’ll get.
“When you give, keep it so quiet your left hand doesn’t know what your right hand is doing.
“Let your giving stay private. Then your Father, who sees what happens in secret, will reward you openly.

“When you pray, don’t copy the hypocrites. They love standing in synagogues and street corners, praying where people can see them. I’m telling you the truth: that attention is all the reward they’ll get.
“But when you pray, go into your private room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is unseen. Your Father, who sees what happens in secret, will reward you openly.
“When you pray, don’t pile up empty phrases like the Gentiles do. They think all those words will make God hear them.
“Don’t copy them. Your Father already knows what you need before you ask him.
“Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
‘Let your Kingdom come. Let your will happen on earth just as it does in heaven.
‘Give us today the bread we need for today.
‘Forgive us for what we owe, just as we forgive those who owe us.
‘Don’t lead us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. The Kingdom, the power, and the glory are yours forever. Amen.’
“If you forgive other people when they wrong you, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.
“But if you don’t forgive others when they wrong you, your Father won’t forgive your wrongs either.

“And when you fast, don’t pull a gloomy face like the hypocrites. They make themselves look miserable so people will know they’re fasting. I’m telling you the truth: that attention is all the reward they’ll get.
“But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
“so people won’t clock that you’re fasting—only your Father, who is unseen, will know. Your Father, who sees what happens in secret, will reward you openly.
“Don’t stack up treasures on earth, where moths and rust wreck them, and thieves break in and steal.
“Stack up treasures in heaven instead, where moths and rust can’t wreck them and thieves can’t break in and steal.
“Where your treasure is, your heart will be there too.
“The eye is the body’s lamp. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
“But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If the light inside you is darkness, that darkness is deep indeed.
“Nobody can serve two masters. You’ll hate one and love the other, or stay loyal to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
“So I’m telling you: don’t be anxious about your life—what you’ll eat or drink—or your body, what you’ll wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
“Look at the birds in the sky: they don’t plant, harvest, or store food in barns, yet your Father in heaven feeds them. Aren’t you worth much more than they are? 🐦
“Can any of you add even one moment to your life by worrying?
“And why stress about clothes? Look at the lilies in the field and how they grow. They don’t work hard or spin thread,
“yet I’m telling you, even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one of them.
“If God dresses the field grass like this—here today, tossed into an oven tomorrow—won’t he clothe you even more, you of little faith?
“So don’t stress and ask, ‘What will we eat?’ ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
“The Gentiles chase after all these things, but your Father in heaven knows you need them.
“Make God’s Kingdom and his righteousness your first pursuit, and all these things will be given to you too.
“So don’t stress about tomorrow. Tomorrow can deal with its own worries. Today already has enough trouble of its own.”
“Don’t judge people, or you’ll be judged too.
“The same standard you use on others will be used on you; the measure you hand out is the measure you’ll get back.
“Why are you spotting the tiny splinter in your brother’s eye, but missing the whole plank in your own?
“How can you tell your brother, ‘Here, let me get that splinter out of your eye,’ when there’s a plank in your own eye?
“Hypocrite! Get that plank out of your own eye first. Then you’ll see clearly enough to help with the splinter in your brother’s eye.
“Don’t give what’s holy to dogs or toss your pearls to pigs. They may trample them, then turn on you and tear you apart.
“Ask, and it will be given to you. Search, and you’ll find. Knock, and the door will open for you.
“Everyone who asks receives; the one who searches finds; and the door opens for the one who knocks.
“If your son asks you for bread, would any of you hand him a stone?
“Or if he asks for a fish, would you hand him a snake?
“Even though you are evil, you know how to give good gifts to your children. So how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
“So treat people the way you want them to treat you. That sums up the Law and the Prophets.
“Go in through the narrow gate. The gate is wide and the road is broad that leads to destruction, and plenty of people take that road.
“But the gate is narrow and the road is tight that leads to life. Only a few find it.
“Watch out for false prophets. They come dressed like sheep, but inside they’re ravenous wolves.
“You’ll recognize them by what their lives produce. Do people pick grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles?
“A good tree produces good fruit; a rotten tree produces bad fruit.
“A good tree can’t produce bad fruit, and a rotten tree can’t produce good fruit.
“Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit gets cut down and thrown into the fire.
“So yes—you’ll recognize them by their fruit.
“Not everyone who calls me ‘Lord, Lord’ will enter Heaven’s Kingdom. The one who does what my Father in heaven wants will enter.
“Many will tell me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, drive out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?’
“Then I’ll tell them, ‘I never knew you. Get away from me, you who practice lawlessness.’
“So everyone who hears these words of mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on rock.
“The rain came down, the floodwaters rose, and the winds slammed into that house. It still didn’t fall, because its foundation was rock.
“Everyone who hears these words of mine but doesn’t act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
“The rain came down, the floodwaters rose, and the winds slammed into that house. It fell—and what a wreck it was!”
When Jesus finished saying all this, the crowds were amazed at his teaching.
He taught with authority, nothing like their scribes.
When Jesus came down from the mountain, huge crowds followed him.
A man with leprosy came up, bowed before him, and said, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
Jesus reached out and touched him. “I choose to. Be clean,” he said. Immediately, the leprosy was gone.
Then Jesus told him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. Go show yourself to the priest and bring the gift Moses commanded as a testimony to them.”
When Jesus entered Capernaum, a Roman army officer came to him, asking for help.
“Lord, my servant is at home, paralyzed and suffering terribly.”
Jesus told him, “I’ll come and heal him.”
The officer answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
“I’m a man under authority too, with soldiers under me. I tell one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and I tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
Jesus was amazed when he heard this. He told the people following him, “I’m telling you the truth: I haven’t found faith this strong anywhere in Israel.
“Many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in Heaven’s Kingdom,
“but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown outside into the darkness. There, people will weep and grind their teeth.”
Jesus told the officer, “Go. Let it happen just as you believed.” His servant was healed at that very hour.
When Jesus came to Peter’s house, he saw Peter’s mother-in-law lying down with a fever.
Jesus touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began serving him.
That evening, people brought him many who were possessed by demons. He drove out the spirits with a word and healed everyone who was sick.
This fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah had said: “He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.”
When Jesus saw the huge crowd around him, he ordered them to cross to the other side.
A scribe came up and said to him, “Teacher, I’ll follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus told him, “Foxes have holes, and birds in the sky have nests. But the Son of Man has nowhere to rest his head.”
Another of his disciples said, “Lord, let me first go and bury my father.”
But Jesus told him, “Follow me. Let the dead bury their own dead.”
Jesus got into a boat, and his disciples followed him.
Suddenly, a violent storm rose on the sea. Waves were covering the boat, but Jesus was asleep.
The disciples went over and woke him up: “Lord, save us! We’re going under!”
He asked them, “Why are you scared, you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and sea, and everything went calm.
The men were stunned: “What kind of man is this? Even the wind and sea obey him!”
When Jesus reached the other side, in the region of the Gergesenes, two men possessed by demons met him. They came out of the tombs, so violent that nobody could pass that way.
They shouted, “What do you want with us, Jesus, Son of God? Did you come to torment us before the appointed time?”
A large herd of pigs was feeding some distance away.
The demons begged him, “If you’re driving us out, send us into that herd of pigs.”
He told them, “Go!” They came out and entered the pigs. Then the whole herd rushed down the steep slope into the sea and died in the water.
The people tending the pigs ran into the city and told everyone what happened, including what had happened to the men who were possessed by demons.
The whole city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
Jesus got into a boat, crossed the water, and came to his own town.
Some people brought him a paralyzed man lying on a mat. When Jesus saw their faith, he told the man, “Take heart, son. Your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is insulting God.”
Jesus knew what they were thinking. “Why are you holding evil thoughts in your hearts?
“Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or ‘Get up and walk’?
“But I’ll show you that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” Then he told the paralyzed man, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
The man got up and went home.
When the crowds saw it, they were amazed and praised God for giving this kind of authority to people.
As Jesus moved on, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow me,” Jesus told him. Matthew got up and followed him.
Later, Jesus was eating in a house when many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.
The Pharisees saw this and asked his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus heard them and said, “People who are well don’t need a doctor; sick people do. 🩺
“Go learn what this means: ‘I want mercy, not sacrifice.’ I didn’t come to call the righteous; I came to call sinners to turn back to God.”
Then John’s disciples came and asked him, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples don’t fast?”
Jesus told them, “Can the groom’s friends mourn while the groom is still with them? The time will come when he’s taken away from them; then they will fast.
“Nobody patches an old garment with cloth that hasn’t shrunk. The patch will pull away and leave an even worse tear.
“And nobody pours new wine into old wineskins. The skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the skins will be ruined. New wine goes into fresh wineskins, and both are kept safe.”
While Jesus was saying this, a leader came, bowed before him, and said, “My daughter has just died. Come lay your hand on her, and she’ll live.”
Jesus got up and went with him, and his disciples went too.
A woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of his robe.
She was thinking, “If I can just touch his robe, I’ll be made well.”
Jesus turned, saw her, and said, “Take heart, daughter. Your faith has made you well.” The woman was healed right then.
Jesus came to the leader’s house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a loud commotion.
He said, “Make some room. The girl isn’t dead; she’s sleeping.” They laughed at him.
After the crowd was sent outside, Jesus went in, took her by the hand, and the girl got up.
News of this spread through the whole region.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, shouting, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
When Jesus went into a house, the blind men came to him. He asked, “Do you believe I can do this?” They said, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched their eyes and said, “Let it happen for you as you believe.”
Their eyes opened. Jesus gave them a strict warning: “See that nobody finds out about this.”
But they went out and spread the news about him all over the region.
As they were leaving, people brought Jesus a man who couldn’t speak because he was possessed by a demon.
When the demon was driven out, the man spoke. The crowds were amazed: “Nothing like this has ever happened in Israel!”
But the Pharisees said, “He drives out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
Jesus traveled through all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.
When he saw the crowds, compassion moved him. They were worn down and scattered, like sheep with no shepherd.
Then he told his disciples, “The harvest is huge, but the workers are few.
“So ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers into his harvest field.”
Jesus called his twelve disciples over and gave them authority to drive out unclean spirits and heal every disease and sickness.
Here are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, called Peter; then his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee; and his brother John;
Philip; Bartholomew; Thomas; Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus; and Lebbaeus, also called Thaddaeus;
Simon the Zealot; and Judas Iscariot, the one who betrayed Jesus.
Jesus sent these twelve out with instructions: “Don’t go among the Gentiles or enter any Samaritan town.
“Go instead to the lost sheep of Israel’s people.
“As you go, preach this: ‘Heaven’s Kingdom is close!’
“Heal the sick, make people with leprosy clean, and drive out demons. You received freely, so give freely.
“Don’t carry gold, silver, or copper in your money belts.
“Don’t take a travel bag, an extra shirt, sandals, or a walking stick. A worker deserves their food.
“When you enter a city or village, find out who there is worthy, and stay at that home until you leave.
“When you enter a home, greet the people there.
“If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it. If it isn’t, let your peace come back to you.
“If anyone won’t welcome you or listen to your words, leave that home or city and shake its dust off your feet.
“I’m telling you the truth: Sodom and Gomorrah will have an easier time on judgment day than that city.
“Look, I’m sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be wise like snakes and innocent like doves. 🐍🕊️
“Watch out for people. They’ll hand you over to councils and whip you in their synagogues.
“You’ll be brought before governors and kings because of me, as a witness to them and to the nations.
“When they hand you over, don’t panic about what to say or how to say it. You’ll be given the words in that moment.
“It won’t be you speaking; it will be your Father’s Spirit speaking through you.
“A brother will hand his brother over to death, and a father will hand over his child. Children will turn against their parents and have them put to death.
“Everyone will hate you because of my name. But the one who keeps going to the end will be saved.
“When they persecute you in one city, escape to the next. I’m telling you the truth: you won’t finish going through Israel’s cities before the Son of Man comes.
“A disciple isn’t above their teacher, and a servant isn’t above their master.

“It’s enough for a disciple to become like their teacher, and a servant like their master. If they called the head of the house Beelzebul, how much more will they say it about the people in his household?
“So don’t fear them. Nothing is covered that won’t be revealed; nothing is hidden that won’t be known.
“What I tell you in the dark, speak in the light. What you hear whispered in your ear, announce from the rooftops.
“Don’t fear those who can kill the body but can’t kill the soul. Fear the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
“Aren’t two sparrows sold for one small coin? Yet not one falls to the ground apart from your Father’s will. 🐦
“Even the hairs on your head are all counted.
“So don’t be afraid. You matter more than many sparrows.
“Everyone who confesses me in front of people, I’ll also confess before my Father in heaven.
“But whoever disowns me in front of people, I’ll disown before my Father in heaven.
“Don’t think I came to bring peace to the earth. I didn’t come to bring peace, but a sword.
“I came to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
“A person’s enemies will be the people in their own household.
“Anyone who loves father or mother more than me isn’t worthy of me. Anyone who loves son or daughter more than me isn’t worthy of me.
“Anyone who won’t take up their cross and follow me isn’t worthy of me.
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it; whoever loses their life for my sake will find it.
“Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
“Whoever welcomes a prophet because they’re a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. Whoever welcomes a righteous person because they’re righteous will receive a righteous person’s reward.
“I’m telling you the truth: whoever gives even one of these little ones a cup of cold water because they’re my disciple won’t lose their reward.”
After Jesus finished instructing his twelve disciples, he left to teach and preach in their towns.
John heard in prison about what the Messiah was doing, so he sent two of his disciples
to ask him, “Are you the one who’s coming, or should we expect someone else?”
Jesus answered them, “Go tell John what you hear and see:
“Blind people see, those who couldn’t walk are walking, people with leprosy are made clean, deaf people hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear the Good News.
“Blessed is the one who doesn’t stumble because of me.”
As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began telling the crowds about John: “What did you go out to the wilderness to see—a reed shaking in the wind?
“What did you go out to see—a man dressed in soft clothes? People in soft clothes live in royal houses.
“So what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes—and more than a prophet.
“This is the one the Scripture talks about: ‘Look, I’m sending my messenger ahead of you. He’ll prepare your way before you.’
“I’m telling you the truth: no one born of a woman has appeared greater than John the Baptizer. Yet the least in Heaven’s Kingdom is greater than he is.
“From the days of John the Baptizer until now, Heaven’s Kingdom has suffered violence, and violent people are trying to seize it by force.
“All the prophets and the Law prophesied up to John.
“If you’re willing to accept it, John is Elijah, the one who was to come.
“If you have ears, listen up!
“What can I compare this generation to? It’s like children sitting in the marketplace, calling out to their friends
“‘We played a sad tune for you, but you didn’t dance. We mourned, but you didn’t grieve.’
“John came without eating or drinking, and people said, ‘He has a demon.’
“The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and people say, ‘Look at him—a glutton, a drunk, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is proved right by her children.”
Then Jesus began calling out the cities where most of his mighty works had happened, because they hadn’t turned back to God.

“How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the mighty works done in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned back long ago, wearing sackcloth and sitting in ashes.
“But I’m telling you, Tyre and Sidon will have an easier time on judgment day than you.
“And you, Capernaum, do you think you’ll be lifted up to heaven? You’ll be brought down to Hades. If the mighty works done in you had happened in Sodom, it would still be here today.
“But I’m telling you, Sodom will have an easier time on judgment day than you.”
At that time Jesus prayed, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from the wise and well-informed and revealed them to little children.
“Yes, Father, this was pleasing to you.
“My Father has handed everything over to me. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to reveal him to.
“Come to me, all of you worn out from work and carrying heavy loads, and I’ll give you rest. 🫶
“Take my yoke on you and learn from me. I’m gentle and humble in heart, and you’ll find rest for your souls.
“My yoke fits well, and my load is light.”
Around then, Jesus walked through grain fields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, so they started picking heads of grain and eating.
The Pharisees saw them and said to Jesus, “Look, your disciples are doing what isn’t allowed on the Sabbath.”
He replied, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
“He went into God’s house and ate the showbread—the bread set out before God. It wasn’t lawful for him or his companions to eat it; only the priests could.
“Or haven’t you read in the Law that priests in the temple break the Sabbath and are still innocent?
“I’m telling you, someone greater than the temple is here.
“If you understood what this means—‘I want mercy, not sacrifice’—you wouldn’t have condemned the innocent.
“The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
Jesus left there and went into their synagogue.
A man with a withered hand was there. They asked Jesus, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” They wanted a reason to accuse him.
He said to them, “If one of you has a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath, won’t you grab it and pull it out?
“A person is worth much more than a sheep. So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” The man stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy like the other one.
But the Pharisees left and plotted how they could destroy Jesus.
Jesus knew what they were planning and withdrew from there. Huge crowds followed him, and he healed them all.
He warned them not to make him known,
so what God had spoken through Isaiah the prophet would come true:
“Look at my servant, whom I chose; my beloved, with whom I’m well pleased. I’ll put my Spirit on him, and he’ll announce justice to the nations.
“He won’t argue or shout. Nobody will hear his voice out in the streets.
“He won’t snap a bruised reed or put out a smoldering wick, until he leads justice to victory.
“The nations will put their hope in his name.”
Then people brought Jesus a man possessed by a demon who was blind and couldn’t speak. Jesus healed him, and the man could both speak and see.
All the crowds were amazed. “Could this be the Son of David?” they asked.
When the Pharisees heard, they said, “This man drives out demons only by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
Jesus knew their thoughts and told them, “Every kingdom fighting itself ends up ruined. No city or household split against itself will stand.
“If Satan drives out Satan, he’s fighting himself. How can his kingdom stand?
“If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, who gives your own sons authority to drive them out? They’ll be your judges.
“But if I drive out demons by God’s Spirit, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
“How can anyone enter a strong man’s house and loot his goods without tying him up first? Then they can plunder his house.
“Anyone who isn’t with me is against me; anyone who doesn’t gather with me scatters.
“So I’m telling you: every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Spirit won’t be forgiven.
“Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven, in this age or the age to come.
“Make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad—the tree is known by the fruit it produces.
“You brood of snakes! How can you, being evil, say anything good? The mouth speaks from whatever fills the heart.
“A good person brings good things out of their good treasure; an evil person brings evil things out of their evil treasure.
“I’m telling you, people will answer on judgment day for every careless word they speak.
“Your words will either show you’re in the right or condemn you.”
Then some scribes and Pharisees answered him, “Teacher, we want you to show us a sign.”
He replied, “An evil and adulterous generation keeps asking for a sign. No sign will be given except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
“Just as Jonah was in the huge fish’s belly for three days and three nights, the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
“The people of Nineveh will stand up at judgment with this generation and condemn it. They turned back to God when Jonah preached, and someone greater than Jonah is here.
“The Queen of the South will rise at judgment with this generation and condemn it. She came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom, and someone greater than Solomon is here.
“When an unclean spirit leaves someone, it wanders through dry places looking for rest but finds none.
“Then it says, ‘I’ll go back to my house—the place I left.’ When it returns, it finds the place empty, swept clean, and put in order.
“So it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself. They move in and live there. That person’s last state is worse than the first. That’s how it will be for this evil generation.”
While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak with him.
Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking to speak with you.”
He answered the person who told him, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
He pointed toward his disciples and said, “Look—my mother and brothers!
“Anyone who does what my Father in heaven wants is my brother, sister, and mother.”
That same day, Jesus left the house and sat beside the sea.
Huge crowds gathered around him, so he got into a boat and sat down. Everyone else stood along the shore.
He taught them many things through stories. “Listen: a farmer went out to scatter seed.
“As he scattered it, some seed landed beside the road. Birds came and ate it up.
“Some landed on rocky ground with little soil. It sprouted fast because the soil wasn’t deep.
“But when the sun came up, it got scorched. With no roots, it dried up.
“Some seed landed among thorns. The thorns grew and choked it.
“Some landed in good soil and produced a harvest: one hundred times as much, some sixty, some thirty. 🌱
“If you have ears, listen!”
The disciples came and asked him, “Why do you teach them through stories?”
He answered, “You’ve been given the chance to understand Heaven’s Kingdom secrets; they haven’t.
“Whoever has will be given more, until they have plenty. But whoever doesn’t have, even what they have will be taken away.
“That’s why I teach them in stories: they look but don’t really see; they hear but don’t really listen or understand.
“Isaiah’s prophecy is coming true in them: ‘You’ll hear and hear, but never understand; you’ll look and look, but never see.

‘These people’s hearts have grown hard. Their ears barely hear, and they’ve shut their eyes. Otherwise, they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back to me, and be healed.’
“But blessed are your eyes, because they see; blessed are your ears, because they hear.
“I’m telling you the truth: many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you’re seeing but never saw it, and wanted to hear what you’re hearing but never heard it.
“So hear what the farmer’s story means.
“When someone hears the message about Heaven’s Kingdom but doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was planted in their heart. That’s the seed beside the road.
“The seed on rocky ground is someone who hears the message and welcomes it right away, all excited,
“but they have no root and don’t last. When trouble or persecution comes because of the message, they stumble immediately.
“The seed among thorns is someone who hears the message, but worries about this age and the trickiness of wealth choke it. They become unfruitful.
“The seed in good soil is someone who hears and understands the message. They truly produce fruit: a hundred times, sixty, or thirty times what was planted.”
Jesus told them another story: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like a man who planted good seed in his field.
“While everyone was asleep, his enemy came, planted weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.
“When the green shoots came up and the grain formed, the weeds showed up too.
“The owner’s servants came and asked, ‘Sir, didn’t you plant good seed in your field? Where did these weeds come from?’
“He told them, ‘An enemy did this.’ The servants asked, ‘Do you want us to go pull the weeds?’
“‘No,’ he said. ‘If you pull the weeds, you might pull up the wheat with them.
“‘Let them grow together until harvest. At harvest time I’ll tell the reapers: First gather the weeds and tie them in bundles to burn; then bring the wheat into my barn.’”
He told them another story: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like a mustard seed a man took and planted in his field.
“It’s the smallest of seeds, but when it grows, it’s bigger than the garden plants and becomes a tree. Birds come and nest in its branches.”
He told them another story: “Heaven’s Kingdom is like yeast a woman mixed into three measures of flour, until all the dough rose.”
Jesus told the crowds all these things in stories. He didn’t say anything to them without a story,
to fulfill what the prophet had said: “I’ll speak in stories; I’ll reveal things hidden since the world began.”
Then Jesus sent the crowds away and went into a house. His disciples came to him: “Explain the story about the weeds in the field.”
He answered, “The one who plants the good seed is the Son of Man.
“The field is the world. The good seed means the children of Heaven’s Kingdom; the weeds mean the children of the evil one.
“The enemy who planted them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
“Just as the weeds are gathered and burned, that’s what will happen at the end of this age.
“The Son of Man will send his angels to clear out everything that causes people to stumble and everyone who practices evil from his Kingdom.
“They’ll throw them into the fiery furnace, where people will weep and grind their teeth.
“Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father’s Kingdom. If you have ears, listen!
“Heaven’s Kingdom is also like treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it again. Overjoyed, he sold everything he had and bought that field.
“Again, Heaven’s Kingdom is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.
“When he found one pearl of great value, he went and sold everything he had and bought it. 💎
“Again, Heaven’s Kingdom is like a net thrown into the sea that catches all kinds of fish.
“When it was full, the fishermen pulled it ashore. They sat down, put the good fish into containers, and threw away the bad ones.
“That’s how it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous,
“and throw them into the fiery furnace, where people will weep and grind their teeth.”
Jesus asked them, “Have you understood all this?” They answered, “Yes, Lord.”
He said, “So every teacher of the Law who becomes a disciple of Heaven’s Kingdom is like a homeowner bringing new and old treasures out of storage.”
When Jesus finished telling these stories, he left that place.
He went to his hometown and taught in their synagogue. The people were amazed: “Where did he get this wisdom and these miracles?
“Isn’t he the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother named Mary? Aren’t James, Joses, Simon, and Judas his brothers?
“And don’t all his sisters live here with us? Where did he get all this?”
They were offended by him. Jesus told them, “A prophet gets respect everywhere except in his hometown and his own house.”
He didn’t do many miracles there because they didn’t believe.
Around that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus.
He told his servants, “This is John the Baptizer. He’s come back from the dead—that’s why these powers are at work in him.”
Herod had arrested John, tied him up, and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
John had kept telling Herod, “You aren’t allowed to have her.”
Herod wanted to kill John, but he was afraid of the crowd because they considered John a prophet.
At Herod’s birthday celebration, Herodias’s daughter danced in front of the guests and pleased him.
So he swore an oath to give her whatever she asked for.
Prompted by her mother, she said, “Bring me John the Baptizer’s head here on a platter.”
The king was distressed, but because of his oath and the guests at his table, he ordered it done.
He sent someone to behead John in prison.
John’s head was brought in on a platter and given to the young woman, who took it to her mother.
John’s disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard, he left by boat for a quiet, out-of-the-way place. The crowds heard where he went and followed on foot from their towns.
When Jesus came ashore and saw the huge crowd, he felt compassion for them and healed their sick.
That evening, the disciples came to him: “This place is deserted, and it’s getting late. Send the crowds to the villages so they can buy food for themselves.”
Jesus told them, “They don’t need to leave. You give them something to eat.”
They said, “All we have here is five loaves and two fish.”
He said, “Bring them here to me.”

He told the crowds to sit on the grass. He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples. The disciples gave the food to the crowds.
Everyone ate and got full. Then they gathered twelve baskets of leftover pieces.
About five thousand men ate, not counting the women and children.
Right away, Jesus made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the crowds away.
After sending everyone away, he went up the mountain by himself to pray. When evening came, he was there alone.
By then the boat was midway across the sea, getting battered by waves because the wind was against it.
During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came toward them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they panicked. “It’s a ghost!” they cried out in fear.
Jesus spoke to them right away: “Take courage! It’s me. Don’t be afraid.”
Peter answered him, “Lord, if it’s you, tell me to come to you on the water.”
Jesus said, “Come!” Peter climbed out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus.
But when Peter noticed how strong the wind was, he got scared. As he started sinking, he shouted, “Lord, save me!”
Jesus immediately reached out, grabbed him, and said, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
When they climbed into the boat, the wind stopped.
Those in the boat bowed before him: “You really are God’s Son!”
After crossing over, they reached the land of Gennesaret.
The people there recognized Jesus and sent word through the whole surrounding region. They brought him everyone who was sick,
and begged him to let them touch just the fringe of his robe. Everyone who touched it was made well.
Then Pharisees and scribes came from Jerusalem to question Jesus:
“Why do your disciples ignore the elders’ tradition? They eat without washing their hands first.”
He replied, “Why do you use your tradition to ignore God’s command?
“God commanded, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must be put to death.’
“But you say, ‘If someone tells their father or mother, “Any support you could have received from me is dedicated to God,”
“they don’t have to honor their father or mother.’ So your tradition has made God’s command powerless.
“Hypocrites! Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you:
“‘These people honor me with their mouths and lips, but their hearts are far from me.
“‘Their worship is empty; they teach human rules as if they were God’s commands.’”
Then Jesus called the crowd over: “Listen up and understand this:
“What goes into the mouth doesn’t make a person unclean. What comes out of the mouth—that’s what makes a person unclean.”
Then the disciples came and said, “Do you know the Pharisees took offense when they heard what you said?”
He answered, “Every plant my Father in heaven didn’t plant will be pulled up by the roots.
“Leave them alone. They’re blind guides leading blind people. If a blind person guides another, both will fall into a pit.”
Peter answered him, “Explain that parable to us.”
Jesus said, “You still don’t get it either?
“Don’t you understand? Whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach and then out of the body.
“But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and that makes a person unclean.
“Evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and insults against God come from the heart.
“Those are what make a person unclean. Eating with unwashed hands doesn’t.”
Jesus left that place and went into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
A Canaanite woman from that region came out, shouting, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is suffering terribly because of a demon!”
Jesus didn’t answer her at all. His disciples came and urged him, “Send her away; she keeps shouting after us.”
He replied, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel’s people.”
But she came, bowed before him, and pleaded, “Lord, help me!”
He answered, “It isn’t right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
“Yes, Lord,” she said, “but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”
Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, your faith is great! Let it happen just as you want.” Her daughter was healed at that very hour.
Jesus left there and went along the Sea of Galilee. He climbed a mountain and sat down.
Huge crowds came to him, bringing people who couldn’t walk, people who were blind or couldn’t speak, people with other disabilities, and many more. They laid them at Jesus’ feet, and he healed them.
The crowd was amazed: people who couldn’t speak were talking, people with disabilities were healed, people who couldn’t walk were walking, and blind people could see. They praised Israel’s God.

Jesus called his disciples over and said, “I feel compassion for this crowd. They’ve stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away hungry; they might collapse on the road.”
The disciples said, “Where would we get enough bread in this deserted place to feed such a huge crowd?”
Jesus asked, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
He took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and handed them to the disciples. The disciples passed them out to the crowd.
Everyone ate and got full. They gathered seven baskets of leftover pieces. 🍞
Four thousand men ate, not counting the women and children.
After sending the crowd away, Jesus got into a boat and went to the region of Magdala.
The Pharisees and Sadducees came to test Jesus. They asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
He answered, “In the evening you say, ‘The weather will be fine—the sky is red.’
“And in the morning you say, ‘Today will be stormy—the sky is red and threatening.’ You know how to read the sky, but you can’t read the signs of the times! Hypocrites!
“An evil and adulterous generation keeps demanding a sign, but no sign will be given except Jonah’s sign.” Then he left them and went away.
When the disciples reached the other side, they realized they’d forgotten to bring bread.
Jesus told them, “Watch out. Be on guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
They started discussing it among themselves: “He says that because we didn’t bring bread.”
Jesus knew what they were saying. “Why are you talking among yourselves about having no bread, you of little faith?
“Don’t you understand yet? Don’t you remember the five loaves for five thousand people, and how many baskets you collected?
“Or the seven loaves for four thousand people, and how many baskets you collected?
“How did you miss that I wasn’t talking about bread? Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Then they understood: he wasn’t warning them about bread yeast, but about the Pharisees’ and Sadducees’ teaching.
When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I, the Son of Man, am?”
They said, “Some say John the Baptizer, some say Elijah, and others say Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
He asked them, “But who do you say I am?”
Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered him, “You’re blessed, Simon son of Jonah. No human being revealed this to you; my Father in heaven did.
“I’m telling you: you are Peter, and on this rock I’ll build my church. The gates of Hades won’t overpower it.
“I’ll give you the keys of Heaven’s Kingdom. Whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”
Then he strictly told the disciples not to tell anyone that he was the Christ.
From then on, Jesus began explaining to his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and be raised on the third day.
Peter took him aside and began correcting him: “God forbid, Lord! That will never happen to you!”
Jesus turned to Peter and said, “Get behind me, Satan! You’re a stumbling block to me. You’re thinking about human things, not God’s things.”
Then Jesus told his disciples, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must deny themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it; whoever loses their life for my sake will find it.
“What does someone gain by winning the whole world but losing their life? What could they trade for their life?
“The Son of Man will come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he’ll repay each person according to what they’ve done.
“I’m telling you the truth: some standing here won’t taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother and led them up a high mountain, by themselves.
Right in front of them, Jesus was transformed. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became bright as light.
Then Moses and Elijah appeared, talking with him.
Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it’s good we’re here. If you want, I’ll make three shelters—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
While he was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them. A voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son, who brings me joy. Listen to him.”
When the disciples heard this, they fell face-down and were terrified.
Jesus came over, touched them, and said, “Get up. Don’t be afraid.”
When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
As they came down the mountain, Jesus ordered them, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”
His disciples asked him, “Why do the scribes say Elijah has to come first?”
Jesus answered, “Elijah does come first and will restore everything.
“But I’m telling you, Elijah has already come. They didn’t recognize him; they did whatever they wanted to him. The Son of Man will suffer at their hands too.”
Then the disciples understood he was talking about John the Baptizer.
When they reached the crowd, a man came to Jesus, knelt down, and said,
“Lord, have mercy on my son. He has seizures and suffers badly. He often falls into the fire and often into the water.
“I brought him to your disciples, but they couldn’t heal him.”
Jesus answered, “Faithless and twisted generation! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me.”
Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy. He was healed at that very hour.
Later, the disciples came to Jesus privately: “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”

He told them, “Because you don’t trust God enough. I’m telling you the truth: if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.
“But this kind doesn’t come out except through prayer and fasting.”
While they were together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be handed over to people.
“They’ll kill him, and he’ll be raised on the third day.” The disciples were deeply grieved.
When they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma temple tax asked Peter, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the temple tax?”
“Yes,” he said. When Peter entered the house, Jesus spoke first: “What do you think, Simon? Who do earthly kings collect customs and taxes from—their own children or strangers?”
Peter answered, “Strangers.” Jesus said, “Then the children are exempt.
“But so we don’t offend them, go to the sea, cast in a hook, and take the first fish you catch. Open its mouth and you’ll find a stater coin. Take it and pay the tax for me and you.”
Right then, the disciples came to Jesus: “Who’s the greatest in Heaven’s Kingdom?”
Jesus called a little child over and stood the child among them.
He said, “I’m telling you the truth: unless you turn around and become like little children, you won’t enter Heaven’s Kingdom.
“Whoever humbles themselves like this child is the greatest in Heaven’s Kingdom.
“Whoever welcomes a child like this in my name welcomes me.
“But whoever trips up one of these little ones who believe in me would be better off with a huge millstone tied around their neck and sunk deep in the sea.
“How terrible for the world, because things that make people stumble will come. They have to come, but how terrible for the person who brings them!
“If your hand or foot makes you stumble, cut it off and throw it away. Better to enter life maimed or disabled than keep both hands and feet and be thrown into the everlasting fire.
“If your eye makes you stumble, tear it out and throw it away. Better to enter life with one eye than keep both and be thrown into fiery Gehenna.
“Don’t look down on even one of these little ones. Their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father in heaven.
“The Son of Man came to save the lost.”
“What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one wanders off, won’t he leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go search for the one that wandered?
“If he finds it, I’m telling you the truth: he rejoices over that one more than over the ninety-nine that didn’t wander away.
“In the same way, your Father in heaven doesn’t want even one of these little ones to perish.
“If your brother sins against you, go talk to him privately and point out what he did. If he listens, you’ve won your brother back.
“If he won’t listen, take one or two others with you, so every matter can be confirmed by two or three witnesses.
“If he refuses to listen to them, bring it before the church. If he won’t listen to the church either, treat him like a Gentile or a tax collector.
“I’m telling you the truth: whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.
“Again, I’m telling you: if two of you on earth agree about anything you ask for, my Father in heaven will do it for you.
“Where two or three gather in my name, I’m there among them.”
Then Peter came and asked him, “Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother when he sins against me? Seven times?”
Jesus answered, “I’m not saying seven times, but seventy times seven.
“That’s why Heaven’s Kingdom is like a king who decided to settle accounts with his servants.
“When he started settling up, they brought him a servant who owed ten thousand talents.
“The servant couldn’t pay. So his master ordered him sold, along with his wife, children, and everything he owned, to cover the debt.
“The servant fell down before him and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. I’ll pay you everything!’
“The master felt compassion, released the servant, and forgave the debt.
“But that servant went out and found a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him by the throat and demanded, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
“His fellow servant fell down and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. I’ll pay you back!’
“But he refused. He went and put him in prison until he paid what he owed.
“When the other servants saw what happened, they were deeply upset. They went and told their master everything.
“Then his master called him in. ‘You wicked servant! I forgave your whole debt because you begged me.
“‘Shouldn’t you have shown mercy to your fellow servant just as I showed mercy to you?’
“His master was furious and handed him over to the torturers until he paid everything he owed.
“My Father in heaven will do the same to each of you unless you forgive your brother sincerely, from your heart.”
When Jesus finished teaching, he left Galilee and went to the Judean region beyond the Jordan.
Huge crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
The Pharisees came to test him: “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?”
He answered, “Haven’t you read that the Creator made them male and female from the beginning?
“He also said, ‘That’s why a man leaves his father and mother, joins his wife, and the two become one flesh.’
“So they’re no longer two, but one flesh. What God has joined together, no human should separate.”
They asked him, “Then why did Moses command us to give a wife a divorce certificate and send her away?”
He said, “Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard. It wasn’t like that from the beginning.
“I’m telling you: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery. Whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery too.”
The disciples said to him, “If that’s how it is for a husband and wife, maybe it’s better not to marry.”
He answered, “Not everyone can accept this teaching—only those it has been given to.
“Some are eunuchs from birth; some were made eunuchs by people; and some became eunuchs for Heaven’s Kingdom. Anyone able to accept this should accept it.”
Then people brought little children to Jesus so he could lay his hands on them and pray. The disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me. Don’t stop them. Heaven’s Kingdom belongs to people like them.”
He laid his hands on them, then left that place.
A man came to him and asked, “Good teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?”
Jesus said, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
“Which ones?” the man asked. Jesus said, “‘Don’t murder. Don’t commit adultery. Don’t steal. Don’t give false testimony.
“‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
The young man told him, “I’ve kept all those since I was young. What am I still missing?”
Jesus said, “If you want to be perfect, go sell what you own and give it to the poor. Then you’ll have treasure in heaven. After that, come follow me.”
When the young man heard that, he went away sad because he owned a lot.
Jesus told his disciples, “I’m telling you the truth: it’s hard for a rich person to enter Heaven’s Kingdom.
“I’ll say it again: it’s easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter God’s Kingdom. 🐪
The disciples were stunned. “Then who can be saved?” they asked.
Jesus looked at them and said, “For people, this is impossible. With God, all things are possible.”
Peter answered, “Look, we left everything and followed you. What will we get?”

Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: when all things are renewed and the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who followed me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging Israel’s twelve tribes.
“Everyone who left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or land for my name will receive a hundred times as much and inherit eternal life.
“But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first.”
“Heaven’s Kingdom is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
“He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
“About nine in the morning, he went out again and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
“He told them, ‘You go work in the vineyard too, and I’ll pay you whatever is fair.’ So they went.
“He went out again around noon and three in the afternoon and did the same.
“About five in the afternoon, he found more people standing there. He asked, ‘Why have you been standing here idle all day?’
“They said, ‘Nobody hired us.’ He told them, ‘You go work in the vineyard too, and I’ll pay you what’s fair.’
“When evening came, the vineyard owner told his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages. Start with the last ones hired and finish with the first.’
“The people hired around five came, and each received a denarius.
“When the first workers came, they expected to get more. But each of them also received a denarius.
“They took the money and complained to the landowner:
“‘These last workers did only one hour, but you paid them the same as us. We carried the day’s load and the scorching heat!’
“He answered one of them, ‘Friend, I’m not cheating you. Didn’t we agree on one denarius?
“‘Take your pay and go. I want to give the last worker the same as I gave you.
“‘Can’t I do what I want with what belongs to me? Are you jealous because I’m generous?’
“So the last will be first, and the first last. Many are called, but few are chosen.”
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside. On the way, he told them:
“We’re going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes. They’ll condemn him to death
“and hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked, whipped, and crucified. On the third day he’ll be raised.”
Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons. She knelt down and asked him for something.
He asked her, “What do you want?” She said, “Promise that my two sons can sit beside you in your Kingdom—one on your right, one on your left.”
Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you’re asking. Can you drink the cup I’m about to drink and be baptized with my baptism?” They said, “We can.”
He told them, “You will drink my cup and be baptized with the baptism I receive. But sitting on my right or left isn’t mine to assign; those places belong to the ones my Father prepared them for.”
When the other ten disciples heard, they were annoyed with the two brothers.
But Jesus called them over: “You know how rulers of the nations boss people around and their powerful people throw their weight around.
“It won’t be like that among you. Whoever wants to become great among you must serve the others,
“and whoever wants to be first among you must become your slave.
“That’s how the Son of Man came—not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As they were leaving Jericho, a huge crowd followed Jesus.
Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard Jesus was passing, they shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
The crowd told them to be quiet, but they shouted even louder: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Jesus stopped, called them over, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said, “Lord, open our eyes.”
Jesus felt compassion for them and touched their eyes. Right away, they could see, and they followed him.
As they came near Jerusalem and reached Bethsphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples ahead.
He told them, “Go to the village in front of you. Right away you’ll find a donkey tied up, with a colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to me.
“If anyone asks what you’re doing, say, ‘The Lord needs them.’ They’ll send them right over.”
This happened to fulfill what the prophet had spoken:
“Tell Daughter Zion, ‘Look, your King is coming to you, humble and riding on a donkey—a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”
The disciples went and did exactly what Jesus told them.
They brought the donkey and colt, laid their clothes over them, and Jesus sat on them.
A huge crowd spread their clothes across the road. Others cut branches from trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds in front of him and behind him kept shouting, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name! Hosanna in the highest!” 🌿
When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up: “Who is this?”
The crowds answered, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”
Jesus went into God’s temple and drove out everyone buying and selling there. He flipped the tables of the money changers and the benches of the people selling doves.
He told them, “Scripture says, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you’ve turned it into a hideout for robbers!”
People who couldn’t walk and people who were blind came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
The chief priests and scribes saw the amazing things he did and heard the children shouting in the temple, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” They were furious.
They asked him, “Do you hear what they’re saying?” Jesus answered, “Yes. Haven’t you read, ‘You brought perfect praise from the mouths of children and nursing babies’?”
He left them, went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there.
In the morning, as Jesus returned to the city, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree beside the road and went over, but found nothing on it except leaves. He said, “May you never produce fruit again!” The tree dried up right away.
When the disciples saw it, they were amazed: “How did that fig tree dry up so fast?”

Jesus answered, “I’m telling you the truth: if you have faith and don’t doubt, you won’t just do what happened to the fig tree. You could tell this mountain, ‘Lift up and drop into the sea,’ and it would happen.
“Whatever you ask for in prayer, believing, you’ll receive.”
When Jesus entered the temple and began teaching, the chief priests and elders came up: “By what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you that authority?”
Jesus answered, “I’ll ask you one question too. If you answer me, I’ll tell you by what authority I do these things.
“John’s baptism—where did it come from, heaven or people?” They discussed it among themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe John?’
“But if we say, ‘From people,’ we’re afraid of the crowd. They all consider John a prophet.”
They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” He told them, “Then I won’t tell you by what authority I do these things either.
“What do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first and said, ‘Son, go work in my vineyard today.’
“The son answered, ‘I won’t.’ But later he changed his mind and went.
“The father went to the second son and said the same thing. He answered, ‘Yes, sir,’ but didn’t go.
“Which son did what his father wanted?” They answered, “The first.” Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God’s Kingdom ahead of you.
“John came showing you the way of righteousness, but you didn’t believe him. The tax collectors and prostitutes did. Even after you saw it, you didn’t change your minds and believe him.
“Listen to another story. A landowner planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, built a tower, rented it to farmers, and went away.
“When it was time for the fruit, he sent his servants to the farmers to collect what was his.
“The farmers seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
“He sent more servants than before, but the farmers treated them the same way.
“Finally, he sent his son, thinking, ‘They’ll respect my son.’
“But when the farmers saw his son, they said, ‘This is the heir. Come on, let’s kill him and take what he’ll inherit.’
“They grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
“So when the vineyard owner comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
They answered, “He’ll destroy those wicked men and rent the vineyard to other farmers, who’ll give him the fruit at harvest time.”
Jesus said, “Haven’t you read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. The Lord did this, and it’s amazing to us’?”
“So I’m telling you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and given to a nation that produces its fruit.
“Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces. If it falls on someone, it will crush them to dust.”
When the chief priests and Pharisees heard these stories, they realized Jesus was talking about them.
They wanted to arrest him, but were afraid of the crowds, who considered him a prophet.
Jesus answered with another story:
“Heaven’s Kingdom is like a king who prepared a wedding feast for his son.
“He sent his servants to call the invited guests, but they refused to come.
“He sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell the guests, “Dinner is ready. I’ve butchered my cattle and fattened calves. Everything’s ready—come to the wedding feast!”’
“But they brushed it off and went their own way—one to his farm, another to his business.
“The rest grabbed the servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
“The king was furious. He sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
“Then he told his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but the people I invited weren’t worthy.
“‘Go to the street crossings and invite everyone you find to the feast.’
“The servants went out on the roads and gathered everyone they found, good and bad alike. The wedding hall filled with guests.
“When the king came in to see the guests, he noticed a man who wasn’t wearing wedding clothes.
“He asked, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ The man had nothing to say.
“Then the king told his servants, ‘Tie his hands and feet, take him out, and throw him into the outer darkness.’ That’s where people will weep and grind their teeth.
“Many are invited, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and planned how to trap Jesus with his own words.
They sent their disciples to him with the Herodians. They said, “Teacher, we know you’re honest and teach God’s way truthfully, without playing favorites.
“So tell us: is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
Jesus knew their bad intentions. “Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?
“Show me the coin used for the tax.” They brought him a denarius.
He asked them, “Whose face and name are on it?”
They said, “Caesar’s.” He told them, “Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give God what belongs to God.”
When they heard this, they were amazed. They left him and went away.
That same day, Sadducees—who say there’s no resurrection—came and questioned him.
They said, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies without children, his brother must marry the widow and raise children for him.’
“There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died without children, leaving his wife to his brother.
“The same happened with the second and third, right through the seventh.
“After them all, the woman died too.
“So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven married her.”
Jesus answered, “You’re mistaken because you don’t know the Scriptures or God’s power.
“In the resurrection, people don’t marry or get married. They’re like God’s angels in heaven.
“About the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read what God told you?
“‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ God isn’t the God of the dead—he’s the God of the living.”
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
One of them, an expert in the Law, tested Jesus with a question:
“Teacher, which commandment in the Law is the greatest?”
Jesus answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your mind.’
“That’s the first and greatest commandment.
“The second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
