“The whole Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question:
“What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said, “David’s.”
He asked, “Then how does David, speaking by the Spirit, call him Lord?
“‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
“If David calls him Lord, how can he be David’s son?”
No one could answer him. From that day on, no one dared ask him any more questions.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and his disciples:
“The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
“So do what they tell you to observe, but don’t copy what they do. They talk it, but don’t live it.
“They tie up heavy loads that are hard to carry and put them on people’s shoulders, but they won’t lift a finger to help.
“They do everything for people to see. They make their prayer boxes wide and their robe fringes extra long.
“They love the best seats at feasts and the front seats in synagogues,
“the respectful greetings in marketplaces, and people calling them ‘Rabbi.’
“But you shouldn’t be called ‘Rabbi,’ because you have one Teacher, the Christ, and you’re all brothers.
“And don’t call anyone on earth ‘Father,’ because you have one Father, who is in heaven.
“Don’t be called leaders either. You have one Leader, the Christ.
“The greatest among you must serve the others.
“Whoever lifts themselves up will be brought low; whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You take over widows’ homes, then cover it with long prayers. So your judgment will be worse.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut Heaven’s Kingdom in people’s faces. You don’t enter yourselves, and you block those who are trying to enter.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel land and sea to make one convert, then make that person twice as much a child of Gehenna as you are.
“How terrible for you, blind guides! You say, ‘If someone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if they swear by the temple’s gold, they’re bound by it.’
“Blind fools! Which is greater—the gold, or the temple that makes the gold sacred?
“You also say, ‘If someone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if they swear by the gift on it, they’re bound by it.’
“Blind people! Which is greater—the gift, or the altar that makes the gift sacred?
“So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and everything on it.
“Whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who lives in it.
“Whoever swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One sitting on it.

“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give a tenth of mint, dill, and cumin, but you’ve neglected the heavier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faith. You should’ve practiced those without neglecting the others.
“You blind guides—you strain out a gnat but swallow a camel! 🐫
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and plate, but inside they’re full of extortion and excess.
“Blind Pharisee! Clean the inside of the cup first, then the outside will be clean too.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You’re like whitewashed tombs: they look beautiful outside, but inside they’re full of dead people’s bones and uncleanness.
“In the same way, you look righteous to people on the outside, but inside you’re full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the graves of righteous people.
“You say, ‘If we had lived in our ancestors’ days, we wouldn’t have joined them in killing the prophets.’
“By saying that, you testify against yourselves: you’re children of the people who killed the prophets.
“Go on, then—finish what your ancestors started.
“You snakes! Brood of vipers! How will you escape Gehenna’s judgment?
“Look, I’m sending you prophets, wise people, and scribes. You’ll kill and crucify some, whip some in your synagogues, and chase them from city to city,
“so that all the righteous blood shed on earth will fall on you—from righteous Abel’s blood to Zachariah son of Barachiah’s blood, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
“I’m telling you the truth: all this will come on this generation.
“Jerusalem, Jerusalem—you kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children, like a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you refused.
“Look, your house is left desolate.
“I’m telling you, you won’t see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name!’”
Jesus left the temple and was heading out. His disciples came up to show Him the temple buildings.
Jesus answered, “You see all this, yeah? I’m telling you the truth: not one stone here will stay stacked on another. Everything will come down.”
Later, while He sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us, when will this happen? What sign will show You’re coming and this age is ending?”
Jesus replied, “Watch out so nobody tricks you.
Plenty people will come using My name, saying, ‘I’m the Christ,’ and they’ll lead many people off track.
You’ll hear about wars and rumors of wars. Don’t panic; these things have to happen, but the end hasn’t arrived yet.
Nation will rise against nation, kingdom against kingdom. There’ll be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in different places.
All this is only the start of the birth pains. 🌱
“Then people will hand you over to be oppressed and killed. Every nation will hate you because you bear My name.
Many will fall away, betray each other, and turn on one another.
False prophets will show up in numbers and lead many astray.
As lawlessness spreads, many people’s love will grow cold.
But the one who holds on to the end will be saved.
This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached throughout the whole world as a witness to every nation. Then the end will come.
“So when you see the desolating horror Daniel the prophet spoke about standing in the holy place—reader, understand what this means—
then the people in Judea should run for the mountains.
If someone’s on the rooftop, don’t go downstairs to grab stuff from the house.
If someone’s out in the field, don’t turn back for a coat.
Heartbreak for pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days.
Pray your escape doesn’t happen in winter or on the Sabbath,
because then the suffering will be terrible—nothing like it since the world began, and nothing like it ever again.
If those days weren’t cut short, nobody would survive. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.
“If anyone tells you, ‘Look, the Christ is here!’ or ‘There He is!’ don’t buy it.
False christs and false prophets will appear, doing huge signs and wonders, trying to mislead even the chosen ones, if that were possible.
“Look, I’ve told you ahead of time.
“So if they say, ‘He’s out in the wilderness,’ don’t go. Or, ‘He’s hidden in the inner room,’ don’t believe them.
Lightning flashes from east to west where everyone can see it; that’s how the coming of the Son of Man will be.
Wherever there’s a carcass, vultures gather. You know how that goes.
“But right after the suffering of those days, the sun will go dark, the moon won’t shine, stars will fall from the sky, and heaven’s powers will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Every people group on earth will mourn, and they’ll see the Son of Man coming on heaven’s clouds with power and great glory.
He’ll send His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they’ll gather His chosen people from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
“Learn this lesson from the fig tree: when its branch turns tender and leaves come out, you know summer is close.
In the same way, when you see all these things, know He’s near—right at the door.
I’m telling you the truth: this generation won’t pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words? They’ll never pass away.
“Nobody knows that day or hour—not heaven’s angels, only My Father.
The Son of Man’s coming will be like the days of Noah.
Before the flood, people were eating, drinking, getting married and arranging marriages, right up to the day Noah entered the ark.
They didn’t realize what was happening until the flood came and swept them all away. That’s how the Son of Man’s coming will be.
Two men will be working in a field: one will be taken, the other left.
Two women will be grinding grain: one will be taken, the other left.
So stay alert, because you don’t know what hour your Lord is coming. 🔔
Think about it: if the homeowner knew what part of the night a thief was coming, they’d stay awake and wouldn’t let the house get broken into.
So be ready too. The Son of Man will come when you least expect Him. ⏳
“Who’s the faithful, wise servant the master put in charge of the household, to give everyone food at the right time?
Blessed is that servant if the master comes home and finds them doing exactly that.
I’m telling you the truth: the master will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.
But what if that bad servant says to himself, ‘My master is taking forever,’
then starts beating the other servants and partying with drunkards?
That servant’s master will arrive on a day he doesn’t expect and at an hour he doesn’t know.
He’ll cut that servant apart and assign him a place with the hypocrites. That’s where people weep and grind their teeth.”
“Then Heaven’s Kingdom will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
Five were foolish; five were wise.
The foolish ones brought their lamps but didn’t bring extra oil.
The wise ones brought oil in jars along with their lamps.
The groom took a while, so all ten got sleepy and nodded off.
Around midnight, someone shouted, ‘Look! The groom’s coming! Come out and meet him!’ 🔔
All the young women woke up and got their lamps ready.
The foolish ones told the wise, ‘Share some oil with us; our lamps are going out.’
The wise replied, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.’
While they were away buying oil, the groom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Later the others came too, calling, ‘Sir, sir, open the door for us!’
But he answered, ‘I’m telling you the truth: I don’t know you.’
So stay alert, because you don’t know the day or hour the Son of Man is coming.
“It’s like a man going on a trip abroad. He called his servants and trusted them with his property.
He gave one five talents, another two, another one—each according to what they could handle. Then he left.
The servant with five talents got to work right away and earned five more.
The one with two did the same and earned two more.
But the servant with one went off, dug a hole, and hid his master’s money.
“After a long time, the master returned and settled accounts with them.
The servant who got five talents brought five more. ‘Master, you trusted me with five talents. Look, I’ve earned five more.’
“His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were trustworthy with a little; I’ll put you in charge of much more. Come share your master’s joy.’
“Then the servant who got two talents came. ‘Master, you trusted me with two talents. Look, I’ve earned two more.’
“His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were trustworthy with a little; I’ll put you in charge of much more. Come share your master’s joy.’
“Then the servant who got one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew you’re a hard man: you harvest where you didn’t plant and gather where you didn’t scatter.
I was scared, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you can have back what’s yours.’
“His master answered, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! So you knew I harvest where I didn’t plant and gather where I didn’t scatter?
Then you should’ve put my money with the bankers. When I came back, I could’ve collected it with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten.
Everyone who has will receive more and have plenty. But from the one who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away.
Throw that useless servant into the darkness outside, where people weep and grind their teeth.’
“When the Son of Man comes in His glory with all the holy angels, He’ll sit on His glorious throne.
Every nation will gather in front of Him, and He’ll separate people from one another, like a shepherd separates sheep from goats.
He’ll put the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.
Then the King will tell the people on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father. Receive the Kingdom prepared for you since the world was founded.
I was hungry, and you gave Me food. I was thirsty, and you gave Me a drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed Me.
I had no clothes, and you clothed Me. I was sick, and you cared for Me. I was in prison, and you came to visit Me.’
“Then the righteous will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You a drink?
When did we see You as a stranger and welcome You, or without clothes and clothe You?
When did we see You sick or in prison and come visit You?’
“The King will answer, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least important of these My brothers, you did for Me.’
“Then He’ll say to the people on His left, ‘Get away from Me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
I was hungry, and you gave Me no food. I was thirsty, and you gave Me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger, and you didn’t welcome Me. I had no clothes, and you didn’t clothe Me. I was sick and in prison, and you didn’t visit Me.’
“Then they’ll answer, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry, thirsty, a stranger, without clothes, sick, or in prison and fail to help You?’
“He’ll answer, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you failed to do for one of the least important of these, you failed to do for Me.’
They’ll go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life.”
When Jesus had finished saying all this, He told His disciples,
“You know Passover is two days away. The Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, legal experts, and elders gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, Caiaphas.
They plotted to seize Jesus by a trick and kill Him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, or the people might riot.”
Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon, who had been a leper.
A woman came with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume. While Jesus was eating, she poured it on His head.
When the disciples saw it, they got upset. “Why waste it like this?
That perfume could’ve sold for a lot and the money gone to the poor!”
Jesus knew what they were saying and replied, “Why are you giving this woman a hard time? She’s done something beautiful for Me.
The poor will always be with you, but I won’t always be here with you.
When she poured this perfume on My body, she was preparing Me for burial.
I’m telling you the truth: wherever this Good News is preached throughout the world, what she did will be told in her memory.”
Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and asked, “What will you give me if I hand Him over to you?” They counted out thirty silver coins for him.
From then on, Judas looked for a chance to betray Jesus.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples asked Jesus, “Where do You want us to prepare the Passover meal for You?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I’ll celebrate Passover at your house with My disciples.”’”
The disciples did what Jesus told them and got the Passover meal ready.
That evening, Jesus was reclining at the table with the Twelve.
While they were eating, He said, “I’m telling you the truth: one of you will betray Me.”
Deeply sad, each one began asking Him, “Surely it isn’t me, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand in the bowl with Me is the one who’ll betray Me.
The Son of Man is going as Scripture says, but how terrible for the one who betrays Him! It would’ve been better for that man if he’d never been born.”
Judas, the one who was betraying Him, asked, “Surely it isn’t me, Rabbi?” Jesus said, “You said it.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples. “Take it and eat; this is My body.”
Then He took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them. “All of you, drink from it,
because this is My blood of the new covenant, poured out for many so their sins can be forgiven.
I’m telling you, I won’t drink this fruit of the vine again until that day I drink it new with you in My Father’s Kingdom.”
After they sang a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus told them, “Tonight you’ll all stumble because of Me. Scripture says, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the flock’s sheep will scatter.’
But after I’m raised, I’ll go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered, “Even if everyone else stumbles because of You, I never will.”
Jesus told him, “I’m telling you the truth: tonight, before the rooster crows, you’ll deny knowing Me three times.”
Peter said, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” All the other disciples said the same.
Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane. He told His disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with Him. He began to feel deep sorrow and anguish.
Then He told them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow, even to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”
He went a little farther, fell face down, and prayed, “My Father, if it’s possible, let this cup pass from Me. Still, let it be what You want, not what I want.”
He came back to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Couldn’t you stay awake with Me for even one hour?
Stay alert and pray so you don’t fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup can’t pass unless I drink it, let Your will be done.”
He came back and found them asleep again; their eyes were so heavy.
He left them, went away again, and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
Then He returned to the disciples and said, “You’re still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.
Get up, let’s go. Look, the one betraying Me is here.”
While He was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived with a large crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders.
The betrayer had arranged a signal: “The man I kiss is the one. Grab Him.”
Right away Judas came to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” Then he kissed Him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then the crowd grabbed Jesus and arrested Him.
One of Jesus’ companions reached for his sword, drew it, and struck the high priest’s servant, cutting off his ear.
Jesus told him, “Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who uses the sword will die by the sword.
Do you think I can’t ask My Father, and He’d send more than twelve legions of angels right now?
But then how would the Scriptures come true, that this has to happen?”
At that moment Jesus said to the crowd, “Did you come out to arrest Me like I’m a robber, with swords and clubs? I sat in the temple teaching every day, and you didn’t arrest Me.
But all this has happened to fulfill what the prophets wrote.” Then all the disciples left Him and ran away.
The people who arrested Jesus took Him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the legal experts and elders had gathered.
Peter followed from a distance to the high priest’s courtyard. He went in and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
The chief priests, elders, and whole council looked for false testimony against Jesus so they could put Him to death.
They couldn’t find any, even though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
and said, “This man said, ‘I can tear down God’s temple and rebuild it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and asked Him, “Aren’t You going to answer? What do You say about these accusations?”
But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest said to Him, “I put You under oath by the living God: tell us if You are the Christ, God’s Son.”
Jesus answered, “You’ve said it. But I tell you this: from now on you’ll see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on heaven’s clouds.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need more witnesses? You heard the blasphemy yourselves.
What’s your verdict?” They answered, “He deserves death!”
Then they spat in His face and punched Him. Others slapped Him,
saying, “Come on, Christ, prophesy to us! Who hit You?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up and said, “You were with Jesus the Galilean too!”
But he denied it in front of everyone: “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
When he went out to the entrance, another person saw him and told the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth too.”
Again Peter denied it, swearing, “I don’t know the man!”
A little later, the people standing there came over to Peter. “You’re definitely one of them; your accent gives you away.”
Then Peter began cursing and swearing, “I don’t know the man!” At once, a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: “Before the rooster crows, you’ll deny Me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
At daybreak, all the chief priests and elders met and planned to have Jesus executed.
They tied Him up, led Him away, and handed Him over to Governor Pontius Pilate.
When Judas, who had betrayed Jesus, saw He was condemned, he regretted it. He brought the thirty silver coins back to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I sinned. I betrayed an innocent man.” They replied, “That’s your problem. Handle it yourself.”
Judas threw the silver into the temple sanctuary, left, and went and hanged himself.
The chief priests picked up the coins. “It’s against the law to put this blood money in the treasury.”
After discussing it, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
That’s why the field has been called “Field of Blood” ever since.
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet came true: “They took the thirty silver coins—the price set on him, the one some of Israel’s people valued—
and they used them to buy the potter’s field, just as the Lord directed me.”
Jesus stood before the governor. Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “That’s what you say.”
When the chief priests and elders accused Him, He didn’t answer.
Then Pilate asked Him, “Don’t You hear all these charges they’re making against You?”
Jesus didn’t answer a single word, and the governor was really amazed.
At the festival, the governor had a custom of releasing one prisoner the crowd chose.
At that time they had a well-known prisoner called Barabbas.
So when the crowd gathered, Pilate asked them, “Who do you want me to release: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
Pilate knew they had handed Jesus over because they were jealous.
While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him a message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man. Today I suffered a lot in a dream because of Him.”
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and have Jesus killed.
The governor asked them, “Which of these two should I release to you?” They shouted, “Barabbas!”
Pilate said, “Then what should I do with Jesus, the one called Christ?” They all shouted, “Crucify Him!”
The governor asked, “Why? What wrong has He done?” But they shouted even louder, “Crucify Him!”
Pilate saw he wasn’t getting anywhere and a riot was starting. So he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. “I’m innocent of this righteous man’s blood. You deal with it.”
All the people answered, “Let His blood be on us and our children!”
Then Pilate released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus whipped and handed Him over to be crucified.
The governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s headquarters and gathered the whole unit around Him.
They stripped Him and put a scarlet robe on Him.
They twisted thorn branches into a crown and set it on His head, then put a stick in His right hand. They knelt in front of Him and mocked Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spat on Him, took the stick, and hit Him on the head.
After they had mocked Him, they took off the robe, put His own clothes back on Him, and led Him away to crucify Him.
As they went out, they met a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.”
There they offered Jesus sour wine mixed with gall. He tasted it but wouldn’t drink it.
After they crucified Him, they divided His clothes among themselves by casting lots.
Then they sat down and kept watch over Him there.
Above His head they posted the charge against Him: “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right and one on His left.
People passing by insulted Him and shook their heads,
saying, “You said You could destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days. Save Yourself! If You’re God’s Son, come down from the cross!”
The chief priests also mocked Him, along with the legal experts, Pharisees, and elders:
“He saved others, but He can’t save Himself. If He’s Israel’s King, let Him come down from the cross now, and we’ll believe in Him.
He trusts God, so let God rescue Him now if He wants Him. He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
The robbers crucified with Him also threw the same insults at Him.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
Around three, Jesus cried out loudly, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” That means, “My God, My God, why have You abandoned Me?”
Some people standing there heard Him and said, “He’s calling Elijah.”
At once one of them ran, got a sponge, soaked it in vinegar, put it on a stick, and offered Him a drink.
The others said, “Leave Him alone. Let’s see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
Jesus cried out once more, loudly, and gave up His spirit.
Suddenly the temple curtain split in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and rocks broke apart.
Tombs opened, and many bodies of God’s holy people who had died were raised to life.
After Jesus was raised, they came out of the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many people.
When the centurion and those guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and everything that had happened, they were terrified. “This really was God’s Son!” they said.
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and cared for Him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too was a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate ordered that it be handed over.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in clean linen.
He placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a large stone across the tomb’s entrance and left.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting across from the tomb.
The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees went together to Pilate.
They said, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was alive, He said, ‘After three days I’ll rise again.’

So order the tomb secured until the third day. Otherwise His disciples might come at night, steal Him, and tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead!’ That last deception would be worse than the first.”
Pilate told them, “You have guards. Go make it as secure as you know how.”
So they went, secured the tomb, and sealed the stone, with the guards posted there.
After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the tomb.
Suddenly there was a powerful earthquake. An angel of the Lord came down from heaven, rolled the stone away from the entrance, and sat on it.
His appearance flashed like lightning, and his clothes were white as snow.
The guards shook with fear and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, “Don’t be afraid. I know you’re looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
He isn’t here. He has risen, just as He said! Come see the place where He lay.
Now go quickly and tell His disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead. He’s going ahead of you to Galilee; you’ll see Him there.’ I’ve told you.”
The women hurried away from the tomb, afraid but overflowing with joy, and ran to tell His disciples.
Suddenly Jesus met them. “Greetings!” He said. They came up, held His feet, and worshiped Him.
Then Jesus told them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell My brothers to head to Galilee. They’ll see Me there.”
While the women were on their way, some of the guards went into the city and reported everything that had happened to the chief priests.
The priests met with the elders and made a plan. They paid the soldiers a large amount of money,
telling them, “Say, ‘His disciples came during the night and stole Him while we were asleep.’
If this reaches the governor, we’ll talk to him and make sure you don’t get in trouble.”
The soldiers took the money and did what they were told. That story spread among the Jews and is still told today.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, though some still doubted.
Jesus came over and told them, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.
So go and make disciples among all nations. Baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
Teach them to obey everything I commanded you. Remember, I’m with you always, right up to the end of the age.” Amen.
